how_chosen: Ten statements that matter most for the book: verdict-level conclusions (S01, S02, S04), evidence gradings of key claims (S02, S03, S04, S05, S07), operational rules tagged DIFFERS/MISSING (S06 rule 9, S07 rule 16, S08 rule 10, S09 rule 20, S10 rule 4, S03 rule 1), and the factual premises of the top test proposals (T1/T5 -> S03, T2 -> S05/S08, T3 -> S06, T4 -> S07). Question numbers Qn in work_c/QUESTIONS.md map to Sn.

statements.question: Q1
statements.topic: Information in short track records; decay of trend returns
statements.note_statement: Trend, carry and relatives are public risk premia with a low Sharpe (his long run 0.5-1), so a few years of results carry no information and nothing can be timed; alpha decay with a 1-2 decade half-life is statistically indistinguishable from noise; average (pre-cost) return roughly halved since 2010, an environmental decay.
statements.note_kind: decay-undetectability: statistical argument (no test); B25: blog backtest (pre-cost)
statements.note_grade: moderate ('Decay undetectable (MT140-C07-4); average return roughly halved since 2010, environmental (B25)': 'sound statistics; B25 pre-cost, small cohorts')
statements.note_location: section 1 item 1 (lines 11-14); section 2 P3 (line 46); section 3 row (line 95); section 7 (f) (lines 216-218)
scorer_remarks: The 0.5-1 figure is in the claim text of MT044-C04-2, not in its quote ('convert your P&L into an annualized sharp ratio').
B25 is pre-cost and from a model-written digest.

statements.question: Q2
statements.note_statement: Vol scaling beats static sizing: B22 FV Sharpe 1.18 vs 1E1S 0.88 on about 100 futures; B31 0.92 vs 0.57, t 3.59 (after costs); B21 0.25 vs 0.19 per instrument; matches Quantica (MT064-C16-2); the skew static sizing buys is worth less than the Sharpe it costs (B17, MT137-C13-2).
statements.note_kind: SHOWN (blog backtests, one system, in sample, digest numbers unverified)
statements.note_grade: moderate-strong ('SHOWN three times, after costs in B31, matches Quantica (MT064-C16-2); one rule family, in sample, digest unverified')
statements.note_location: section 1 item 2 (lines 15-16); section 2 sizing chain (lines 53-56); section 3 row (line 84)
scorer_remarks: B22's 1.18 is FV (continuous forecast + vol targeting); the like-for-like binary comparison is BV 1.15 vs 1E1S 0.88, so 1.18 vs 0.88 mixes two effects.
B21 is gross of costs and instrument-level; MT064-C16-2 is a Quantica result reported by Carver (cocoa example).

statements.question: Q3
statements.topic: Continuous (non-binary) forecasts; forecast scaling and cap
statements.note_statement: Forecast = scaled risk-adjusted expected return, average absolute 10, cap +/-20, non-binary; forecast strength predicts risk-adjusted return (B04 pooled first-to-last t 35.7, carry 40.9) yet adds only 0.03 Sharpe over a binary position (B22 FV 1.18 vs BV 1.15); extreme buckets flatten or revert, hence the cap (B04, B05).
statements.note_grade: direction strong, size weak ('overlapping returns inflate the t-stats; Sharpe gain over binary 0.03')
statements.note_location: section 1 item 2 (line 17); section 2 forecast chain (lines 58-60); section 3 row (line 86); section 4 rule 1 (line 106); T1 and T5 (lines 157-161, 190-195)
scorer_remarks: The overlap caveat in B04 is marked in the digest as 'Digest note (not from the post)'.

statements.question: Q4
statements.topic: Holding portfolio risk at target versus letting it float with forecast strength
statements.note_statement: Let book risk float with aggregate forecast strength: forcing constant risk cuts Sharpe 0.93 to 0.64 (B03); live, risk falls by itself when forecasts weaken: half of target in June 2024, a third in 2025-26 (MT160-C03-1, MT196-C06-3); risk at a third of target signals a trendless market (MT106-C05-X2).
statements.note_grade: moderate ('one system, 20 instruments; mechanism matches B04')
statements.note_location: section 1 item 2 (line 18); section 2 forecast chain + decision process (lines 60, 77-78); section 3 row (line 88); section 4 rule 5 (line 110); section 7 (lines 211-212)
scorer_remarks: B03 also gives forecast-adjusted 0.87 (removing only the correlation factor); the author would not implement it.

statements.question: Q5
statements.topic: Cost budget, per-trade cost ceiling, live vs model costs
statements.note_statement: Speed limit: annual cost <= 0.13 Sharpe units and <= a third of pre-cost Sharpe; per-trade cost <= 0.01 to trade an instrument; costs in the backtest from day one; live costs just under 100 bp, within 1-2 bp of the model.
statements.note_kind: cost arithmetic observable; one-third rule a heuristic (ASSERT)
statements.note_grade: strong ('costs are observable; the one-third rule is a heuristic (ASSERT)')
statements.note_location: section 1 item 2 (line 18); section 2 costs chain (lines 65-66); section 3 row (line 89); section 4 rule 8 (line 113)
scorer_remarks: MT106-C07-7 claim says costs were within 1-2 bp 'of the prior year, validating the cost model'; quote: 'my costs are exactly in line where I'd expect them to be'. The note's 'within 1-2 bp of the model' is a reading to check.
B26 gives the per-trade ceiling as ~0.007-0.01 SR.

statements.question: Q6
statements.note_statement: No-trade buffer: skip a change under 10% of a standard position, wider for expensive instruments; or a portfolio tracking-error buffer of 10% of target; trade to the buffer edge; expected turnover cut 20-30% (B27: EWMAC4 61.8 -> 49.8, digest, unverified). MISSING in our book.
statements.note_kind: rule stated by Carver (ASSERT for the per-instrument 10%); B13/B27 blog backtests
statements.note_grade: not graded in section 3 (B27 marked 'digest, unverified')
statements.note_location: section 2 costs chain (line 67); section 4 rule 9 (line 114); T3 (lines 172-179)
scorer_remarks: B27 lists S&P500 EWMAC4 turnover as forecast/raw/buffered 61.8/52.6/49.8: buffering alone takes raw 52.6 to 49.8 (about -5%); 61.8 -> 49.8 compares forecast turnover with buffered position turnover. The note's 20-30% cut citing 61.8 -> 49.8 is a reading to check.
MT026-C11-1: the fixed 10% is a simplification suited to retail single-lot trades.

statements.question: Q7
statements.topic: Attenuating trend forecasts by volatility regime
statements.note_statement: Attenuate momentum forecasts in high vol: L = 2 - 1.5Q, Q = percentile of current vol in its 10-year history; +0.04 to +0.09 net Sharpe per rule (carry p 0.32); a SHOWN Carver rule with a mechanism (vol mean reversion whipsaws momentum). MISSING in our book.
statements.note_grade: weak-moderate ('overlapping daily data, cutoffs by eye, weaker at a 3-day lag, motivated by 2020')
statements.note_location: section 3 row (line 91); section 4 rule 16 (line 121); T4 (lines 181-188); section 5 inside-unit (b) (lines 141-142)
scorer_remarks: B24 reasoning: 'No mechanism was established; commenters suggested vol mean reversion whipsawing fast systems'. The note's 'with a mechanism' (line 188) is a reading to check.
Carry p 0.32 is the Medium-vs-High regime difference; the paired attenuation test for carry is p 0.176.
B06: his live system attenuates momentum-style forecasts when vol is above its historic level; MT010-C16-4: he will not implement VIX-based speed changes.

statements.question: Q8
statements.note_statement: Delay test: fills one or two days late; a slow system must be insensitive to a one-day fill delay; over 0.01 Sharpe lost = sensitive, so trade slower or use intraday data.
statements.note_kind: rule of thumb stated by Carver (no test result given)
statements.note_location: section 2 costs chain (lines 67-68); section 4 rule 10 (line 115); T2(a) (lines 164-165)
scorer_remarks: The 0.01 threshold is in the claim text, not in the quote of MT026-C07-1.

statements.question: Q9
statements.note_statement: Drawdown should be read in Sharpe units and is not a separate criterion: it adds nothing beyond Sharpe and history length; the worst drawdown grows with time run; a 50% drawdown would still be a real concern, which the note judges consistent (outside what Sharpe and length predict).

statements.question: Q10
statements.topic: Instrument diversification multiplier and estimation windows
statements.note_statement: IDM from 6-month EW correlation of subsystem P&L and 1-month vol, estimated separately; set below the estimate; positions multiplied about 4-5x to reach target; vol is predictable (R2 0.35 month to month), correlation less so (0.2-0.25). DIFFERS from our book.
statements.note_kind: practice stated by Carver; R2 figures stated in interview (no test shown)
